[LLEX.9.7] **Which code a refusal carries.** [LLEX.9.5] refuses every reserved
word at every naming site with one rule; the diagnostic the compiler reports is
chosen by the word and the site, the first matching row applying:

| Word | Declared as | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `cooldown`, `retain`, `nocooldown` or `as` — a call or emit control-plane modifier | anything | `DS_VALIDATE_RESERVED_META_KWARG` |
| a word [LLEX.9.6] reserves as `type` | a schema, a unit or an `opaque type` | `DS_VALIDATE_RESERVED_TYPE_NAME` |
| a word [LLEX.9.6] reserves as `builtin` | a binding, a `let` or a `const` | `DS_VALIDATE_RESERVED_BUILTIN_NAME` |
| a word [LLEX.9.6] reserves as `aggregation` or `alias`, or any of `p1` … `p99` | a slot | `DS_VALIDATE_COMPANION_SLOT_COLLISION` ([LSER.6.6.1]) |
| any other reserved word | anything | `DS_VALIDATE_HARD_KEYWORD_NAME` |

The modifier row names the four words directly because they are not one class on
[LLEX.9.6]: the engine gives each a meaning at a call or an emit, and a
same-named declaration — a service kwarg above all — would be bound to the
modifier rather than to the author's name.
